(a) Short Title.—This Act may be cited as the “Darfur Peace and Accountability Act of 2006”.  
    (b) Table of Contents.—The table of contents of this Act is as follows: 

Sec. 1. 
Short title; table of contents. 

Sec. 2. 
Definitions. 

Sec. 3. 
Findings. 

Sec. 4. 
Sense of Congress. 

Sec. 5. 
Sanctions in support of peace in Darfur. 

Sec. 6. 
Additional authorities to deter and suppress genocide in Darfur. 

Sec. 7. 
Continuation of restrictions. 

Sec. 8. 
Assistance efforts in Sudan. 

Sec. 9. 
Reporting requirements.

fable.w: This section only gives the Act's short title and lists its section headings; it sets up no process that brings any party outside the federal government into a federal decision. The tempting reading is that headings such as "Reporting requirements" or "Sense of Congress" signal procedure, but they are only table-of-contents entries with no operative text. Reports to Congress would in any case stay inside the federal government.

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of the short title and a table of contents for the Act. It does not contain any substantive provisions requiring consultation, public comment, advisory committees, or other forms of participation by non-federal entities. It is purely structural boilerplate.

opus.w: This section only gives the Act's short title and its table of contents. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. Headings like "Reporting requirements" or "Sense of Congress" are just labels, and reports usually go to Congress, which is inside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: This section consists only of the short title and a table of contents for the Act. It does not contain any operative language requiring or recommending consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government. While the table of contents lists sections like 'Sense of Congress' or 'Reporting requirements,' these are internal legislative actions or reports to Congress (inside the government), not participation by outsiders.

qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "Sense of Congress" or "Findings" implies some form of public input or legislative deliberation that counts as participation. However, these are internal legislative expressions of opinion or fact-finding by Congress (which is inside the federal government) and do not involve consulting with outside parties before a decision is made. The section itself is merely a table of contents and short title, containing no operative language regarding participation.
